conclusion: The measured gain is 10.9% RPM, not a hypothetical animation speedup. Both arms process the same 10,102,214 prompt tokens. Exact uncached work is 1,004,038 vs 1,005,062 tokens. The trace explains the scheduling dependency; the unprofiled run determines the performance result. This bounded 256-request comparison does not reproduce the earlier 22.3% gain from a different 2,048-request screening run.
payload_explanation: The captured return tensors are only 8–104 bytes per microbatch. Every observed result payload contains next_token_ids, an int64 vector: 8 bytes per request in that batch. The host send API median is 0.477 ms across both diagnostic captures. This includes API/metadata/enqueue work and profiling overhead, not just wire time. By contrast, one actual 8K forward proxy can include BF16 hidden states, BF16 residuals and int32 DSA top-k indices. Those are a different message direction and payload.
observed_mechanism:
The extra two slots are directly visible

  • Depth 0: 37 matched microbatches across every rank; 270,355 actual newly computed tokens. PP0 reaches 4 outstanding microbatches and submits up to 3 later microbatches before processing an older result. All ranks finish CPU processing of these batches within 7.160 seconds of first PP0 submission.
  • Depth 2: 35 matched microbatches across every rank; 270,355 actual newly computed tokens. PP0 reaches 6 outstanding microbatches and submits up to 5 later microbatches before processing an older result. All ranks finish CPU processing of these batches within 6.283 seconds of first PP0 submission.

GPU coverage is incomplete in the depth-2 export, so no whole-window GPU-coverage or MFU comparison is valid. A smaller gap between useful submissions is consistent with more scheduling lookahead; raw wait durations also change because batch composition and profiler overhead change. Do not add nested host waits to GPU time or interpret the difference as an isolated NVLink improvement.

Not a blanket single-request latency win: in the matched sequential warmup, TTFT median was 1.279 s at depth 0 and 1.508 s at depth 2. Those warmup prompts differ from the timed backlog workload, so this is a workload-specific observation, not an isolated concurrency sweep.
